title: How to Plan the Right Amount of Office Space
excerpt: Plan office space from activities, attendance, accessibility and growth scenarios instead of relying on one universal ratio.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: How to Plan Office Space for Your Team | YOS
metaDescription: A practical method for planning office space around attendance, activities, accessibility and future change.
body:
There is no single space-per-person number that suits every business. The right area depends on how people work, when they attend and what the workplace needs to support.

## Start with attendance, not headcount alone

Map expected attendance by day, team and work pattern. Include visitors, contractors, new starters and peak events.

## List the activities

Count focused work, collaboration, confidential conversations, client meetings, training, storage, reception, amenities and support spaces. Consider acoustic and technology needs.

## Allow for circulation and building constraints

A quoted floor area does not all become usable work settings. Columns, cores, access paths, services and the shape of the tenancy affect efficiency.

## Check accessibility and compliance

Engage qualified advisers to assess applicable building, accessibility, safety and planning requirements. Do not treat a generic ratio as compliance advice.

## Test scenarios

Model the current need, a realistic growth case and a contraction or flexible-use case. Compare the cost and operational effect of each.

## Validate before committing

Test-fit shortlisted premises and verify measurements, services and approval pathways.
